title: A line-bundle section nonvanishing on a finite set of a quasi-affine scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning that every open covering has a finite subcover, admitting an open immersion into an affine scheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and let $E\subseteq |X|$ be a finite set of points, not necessarily closed. Then there exists $s\in\Gamma(X,L)$ whose germ has nonzero image in $L_x/\mathfrak m_x L_x$ for every $x\in E$, where $\mathfrak m_x$ is the maximal ideal of the local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and $\kappa(x)=\mathcal O_{X,x}/\mathfrak m_x$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. Empty $X$ and empty $E$ are allowed; no Noetherianity, reducedness or irreducibility is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0F20, lemma-quasi-affine-invertible-nonvanishing-section, with W=X and retaining the nonvanishing conclusion. Quasi-affine means quasi-compact and isomorphic to an open of an affine scheme, as in definition-quasi-affine.

proof.text: Fix an open immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow Y$ with $Y$ affine, as in the hypotheses. Apply [lem-a1-quasi-affine-open-principal-comparison-cover] with $U=V=X$ and the identity open immersion. Its last sentence gives a cover of $X$ by affine opens $X_g=\{x:g_x\in\mathcal O_{X,x}^{\times}\}$ for global functions $g$. By [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function] these are exactly the nonvanishing loci of the sections $g$ of $\mathcal O_X$. The module $\mathcal O_X$ is invertible by the identity rank-one trivialization [def-sc-invertible-module]. Hence, taking tensor exponent $1$ at every point and using the assumed quasi-compactness, [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] says that $\mathcal O_X$ is ample.

source.place: Tag 0F20, base case: use of Tag 01QE (properties-lemma-quasi-affine-O-ample); its forward implication here follows directly from the basic-open cover supplied by Tag 0ARY (properties-lemma-cartesian-diagram-quasi-affine), proof

proof.text: By [def-sc-invertible-module], $L$ is quasi-coherent and isomorphic to $\mathcal O$ on each trivializing open. Each such isomorphism is a surjection from one copy of $\mathcal O$, so $L$ is of finite type by [pqf-def-coherent]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-twist-global-generation] with ample module $\mathcal O_X$ and finite type quasi-coherent module $L$. Choose an integer $d\geq\max(1,d_0)$. The conclusion gives a finite global generating family for $L\otimes\mathcal O_X^{\otimes d}$. This module is canonically $L$: multiplication of the scalar factors sends $m\otimes a_1\otimes\cdots\otimes a_d$ to $(a_1\cdots a_d)m$, with inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1\otimes\cdots\otimes1$. These balanced maps commute with restrictions, hence induce inverse maps of the sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Transporting the generating family through this isomorphism proves that $L$ is globally generated.

source.place: Tag 0F20, base case: global generation from Tag 01Q3 (properties-proposition-characterize-ample), implication (1) to (7), with ample module O_X

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-global-generation-nonvanishing-cover] to $L$ and the global generation just obtained. Its asserted cover means that for every $z\in X$ there is $t\in\Gamma(X,L)$ with $t_z\notin\mathfrak m_zL_z$, equivalently $t(z)\ne0$ in $L_z/\mathfrak m_zL_z$. Here and below $u(y)$ denotes the residue value of a section $u$ at $y$.

source.place: Tag 0F20, base case: global generation gives a section nonvanishing at x_1; Modules Tags 01AM (definition-globally-generated) and 01CY (lemma-s-open)

proof.text: We prove the conclusion by strong induction on the cardinality of the finite set $E$, keeping $X$ and $L$ fixed. If $E=\varnothing$, choose the zero global section. Its required nonvanishing condition is vacuous. This also settles empty $X$.

source.place: Tag 0F20, proof, empty case and induction on the number of points

proof.text: Assume $E$ is nonempty and the conclusion holds for smaller finite subsets of $X$. If distinct $x,y\in E$ satisfy $y\in\overline{\{x\}}$, apply induction to $E\setminus\{x\}$. Its section $s$ is nonzero at $y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes], $X_s=\{w:s(w)\ne0\}$ is open. Since $y\in\overline{\{x\}}$, every open containing $y$ contains $x$, so $s(x)\ne0$ as well. This proves the conclusion in this case. It remains to treat $E$ with no specializations between distinct points.

source.place: Tag 0F20, induction step: remove x_i if x_i specializes to another point x_j; openness is Modules Tag 01CY (lemma-s-open)

Choose $z\in E$ and put $F=E\setminus\{z\}$. By induction choose $s\in\Gamma(X,L)$ nonzero on $F$. If $s(z)
e0$ we are done, so assume $s(z)=0$. For every $x\in F$ we have $z
otin\overline{\{x\}}$. The open immersion $j$ is a homeomorphism onto an open subset [def-weil-open-immersion]. An open neighborhood of $z$ missing $x$ therefore maps to an open neighborhood of $j(z)$ in $Y$ missing $j(x)$. Thus $j(z)
otin\overline{\{j(x)\}}$ in $Y$. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-finite-point-scalar-separation] on the affine scheme $Y$ to $j(F)$ and $j(z)$. It gives $a\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ with $a(j(x))=0$ for $x\in F$ and $a(j(z))
e0$. Set $f=j^\#(a)\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. By the open-subscheme identification in [def-weil-open-immersion], its germs are those of $a$ under the local-ring isomorphisms $\mathcal O_{Y,j(w)}\simeq\mathcal O_{X,w}$. The induced residue-field isomorphisms [def-weil-residue-field] give $f(x)=0$ on $F$ and $f(z)
e0$.

source.place: Tag 0F20, induction step: choose a section vanishing at the earlier points and nonvanishing at the new point; the scalar separator is obtained on the ambient affine scheme and restricted to X

proof.text:
Choose $t\in\Gamma(X,L)$ with $t(z)
e0$ by step 3 and put $v=s+ft$. Germ maps and quotient maps respect addition and scalar multiplication, so $v(w)=s(w)+f(w)t(w)$ for every $w\in X$. For $x\in F$, this is $s(x)
e0$. At $z$ it is $f(z)t(z)$, since $s(z)=0$. The nonzero element $f(z)$ of the field $\kappa(z)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is invertible; if $f(z)t(z)=0$, multiplying by its inverse would give $t(z)=0$, a contradiction. Thus $v(z)
e0$, and $v$ works on all of $E$. This completes the induction, including $F=\varnothing$.
